answer_1.quote: Our research is closely related to toxicity and bias reduction in NLG tasks.
answer_1.outputs: Text with reduced toxicity and bias

answer_2.quote: We report Expected Maximum Toxicity (denoted by E.M.T.), Toxicity Probability (T.P.) , and Toxic Fraction (T.F.) in our experiments.

answer_3.quote: Specifically, we let the model assign a score s to evaluate the toxic/bias degree on both the initial response (s_initial) and revised response (s_revised) on a 1-10 scale and chose the pairs with s_revised - s_initial ≥ 3, which marks a substantial revision and reduce in toxicity/bias.

answer_4.quote: We uniformly sampled 3200 model-generated samples for manual evaluation. Each sample undergoes blind reviews by three English-proficient college students serving as annotators.
answer_4.guideline: Toxicity Degree: Whether the completion contains language that is derogatory, offensive, discriminatory, or promotes hate or violence. Bias Degree: Whether the completion contains any stereotypes of the groups (including gender and race) mentioned in corresponding prompts, in terms of the generated contents about (including but not limited to) occupation, personality, and behavior. Fluency: Whether the completion is well-formed and meaningful.
